options.counterfactual: Monotone sequential completeness of finite AW*-factors is an established theorem, rather than an unresolved structural assertion.
options.approach: Audit the precise distinction between normality, monotone completeness, and monotone sequential completeness for AW*-algebras. Identify whether a standard theorem applies directly to the definition in the problem, which would force the set to be empty.

options.counterfactual: Monotone sequential completeness of finite AW*-factors is an established theorem, rather than an unresolved structural assertion.
options.approach: Attempt to reconstruct a sequential completeness proof using spectral projections, finite continuous dimension, and bounded quasitracial completeness. Concentrate on the missing implication that a bounded increasing sequence is quasitracially Cauchy.

options.counterfactual: Monotone sequential completeness of finite AW*-factors is an established theorem, rather than an unresolved structural assertion.
options.approach: Investigate whether countable decomposability of the projection lattice supplies a sequential version of an order-completeness theorem. Separate this possibility from the substantially stronger claim about arbitrary increasing nets.

options.counterfactual: Every finite 2-quasitrace sends the terms of a positive series with bounded partial sums to zero, even without any AW*-algebra assumption.
options.approach: Seek a quantitative exhaustion inequality for positive contractions whose sum is at most the identity. A bound forcing the minimum quasitrace value to vanish as the number of summands grows would exclude every positive increment size.

options.counterfactual: Every finite 2-quasitrace sends the terms of a positive series with bounded partial sums to zero, even without any AW*-algebra assumption.
options.approach: Study the completely positive map from c0 obtained by sending its coordinate projections to the successive differences. Investigate whether nuclearity of c0 and the matrix-extension axiom for a 2-quasitrace imply the required vanishing.

options.counterfactual: Every finite 2-quasitrace sends the terms of a positive series with bounded partial sums to zero, even without any AW*-algebra assumption.
options.approach: Investigate random-sign sums of the positive differences, all of which are contractions. Look for a quasitracial cotype or square-function estimate that converts this uniform norm bound into decay of the individual quasitrace values.

options.counterfactual: There exists a finite AW*-factor with a faithful normalized 2-quasitrace containing a bounded increasing sequence whose successive differences all have the same positive quasitrace.
options.approach: Start from such a sequence and investigate transformations that increase its increment value while preserving the order bound. Determine whether matrix amplification, compression to corners, or operator-monotone functional calculus identifies the sharp endpoint of the resulting interval.

options.counterfactual: There exists a finite AW*-factor with a faithful normalized 2-quasitrace containing a bounded increasing sequence whose successive differences all have the same positive quasitrace.
options.approach: Analyze the candidate endpoint one half. Equality in the elementary upper bound imposes strong spectral-distribution constraints, which might either rule out that endpoint or reveal a canonical construction.

options.counterfactual: There exists a finite AW*-factor with a faithful normalized 2-quasitrace containing a bounded increasing sequence whose successive differences all have the same positive quasitrace.
options.approach: Check whether quasitrace normality on existing suprema automatically rules out a least upper bound for this sequence. If it does, the remaining task reduces to constructing the positive differences rather than separately verifying the order-theoretic requirement.
